title: U.S. House · Michigan's 3rd District
area: Michigan's 3rd Congressional District — Grand Rapids and central-western Michigan.

context.text: Cook Political Report rated Michigan's 3rd District D+4 for the 2026 cycle. Kamala Harris won the district 53.1%–45.2% in 2024.
Incumbent Hillary Scholten was unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary. Terri DeBoer defeated Ryan Cushman in the Republican primary with 78.6% of the vote.

candidates.name: Hillary Scholten
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Scholten is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 3rd District, first elected in 2022. A fourth-generation West Michigander, she worked as a social worker and then as an immigration attorney, including at the U.S. Department of Justice's Board of Immigration Appeals and the Michigan Immigrant Rights Center. She is seeking a third term.

background.text: Born in 1982 in Michigan and raised in the Hudsonville area; her official biography describes her as a fourth-generation West Michigander whose mother was a public school teacher. According to Wikipedia, her father was a sports journalist at The Grand Rapids Press.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Gordon College and a law degree from the University of Maryland School of Law. Sources differ on the graduation years, so they are omitted.

Began her career as a social worker, working with people affected by housing and homelessness issues, according to her official biography; her campaign site says she was a case worker for the AIDS Action Committee.

After law school clerked for the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit in its unit focused on immigration, then joined the U.S. Department of Justice through the Attorney General's Honors Program, working on immigration and civil rights matters.

Served as an attorney adviser with the Justice Department's Board of Immigration Appeals (2013-2017, per Wikipedia), then as a staff attorney at the Michigan Immigrant Rights Center and as senior counsel at Miller Johnson; her campaign site also lists volunteer work as an attorney for the Time's Up Legal Defense Fund.
Ran for the 3rd District in 2020 and lost to Republican Peter Meijer, 47% to 53%.

Won the seat in 2022, defeating Republican John Gibbs 55% to 42%, and took office in January 2023; her official biography says she is the first woman and mother to represent the district. Wikipedia reports she was re-elected in 2024 with 53.7% of the vote.
Committee assignments for 2025-2026: Small Business and Transportation and Infrastructure.
According to her official biography she lives on the southeast side of Grand Rapids, where she is raising two sons.
Was unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Leads the Lowering Costs Caucus and has pushed the administration to address rising energy prices, citing tariffs and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act as factors straining household budgets.

Says Congress must overhaul the immigration system, citing her background as an immigration attorney, and cosponsored the bipartisan Dignity Act to combine border security with a pathway to legal status for undocumented immigrants already in the country.
priorities.quote: Congress must act now to reform our immigration system. It's time to allow hardworking families to move out of the shadows and into the full light of the American dream.

priorities.text: Says everyone deserves access to high-quality reproductive health care and has hosted local roundtables on the issue.
priorities.quote: Everyone deserves access to the high-quality reproductive care they need.

positions.summary: A member of the Pro-Choice Caucus, says abortion rights need to be federally codified and criticized a Supreme Court decision for leaving emergency abortion access unresolved.
positions.quote: For the first time ever, women today have less rights than our mothers and grandmothers. Reproductive care is health care, and pregnant people should not have to be at death's door to receive the care they need to stay alive.

positions.summary: Says gun safety laws that keep firearms out of the hands of abusers are needed to protect women, in a statement on a bill addressing violence against women.
positions.quote: what we really need to move the needle on protecting women are gun safety laws to keep firearms out of abusers' hands

positions.summary: Cosponsored the bipartisan Dignity Act, which pairs border security and infrastructure funding with a pathway to legal status for undocumented immigrants already living in the U.S. and new legal pathways for asylum seekers and economic migrants.
positions.quote: This historic bipartisan legislation would address border security and infrastructure challenges, tackle critical workforce development issues, create legal status for undocumented immigrants already living in the United States, establish new pathways for asylum seekers, and create new legal pathways for economic migrants and unaccompanied minors.

positions.summary: Says she defends the Affordable Care Act and works to expand it, along with capping prescription drug and insulin costs.
positions.quote: I vote to cap the cost of critical prescription drugs and insulin, and I defend the Affordable Care Act and work every day to expand on it.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves on the House Committee on Small Business (Contracting and Infrastructure; Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Workforce Development; Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains) and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation; Water Resources and Environment).
Cosponsored the Dignity Act of 2025, bipartisan immigration legislation addressing border security, a pathway to legal status for undocumented immigrants, and new legal immigration pathways.

candidates.name: Terri DeBoer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 78.6% of the vote

summary.text: DeBoer is a longtime West Michigan television meteorologist running as the Republican nominee for Michigan's 3rd District. She describes herself as an outsider and says her priorities include lowering the cost of living, securing the border and community safety.

background.text: Born at Fort Dix, New Jersey, and raised in a military family according to her campaign website; earned a high school diploma from C.M. Russell High School.
Told Fox News she became interested in politics after hearing Ronald Reagan speak in person during her senior year of high school.
Began in broadcast journalism as a news reporter before moving to meteorology in the early 1990s, according to Fox News.
Has forecast weather on West Michigan television for more than 30 years, at WWMT-TV, WOOD-TV and FOX-17 (WXMI), where she returned in 2024 and left in early 2026.
Inducted into the Michigan Emmy Silver Circle; her campaign website also describes her as an author.
Has served on the boards of the Mental Health Foundation of West Michigan and the Grand Rapids Griffins Youth Foundation, and on the Millennium Park Commission.
Lives in Byron Center and describes herself as a wife, mother and grandmother.
Announced her candidacy in March 2026 and won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 78.6% of the vote over Ryan Cushman.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website located; background limited to what Ballotpedia's biography section documents.

candidates.name: Joe Jock

summary.text: Jock is the Green Party nominee for Michigan's 3rd District, advancing from the Green Party convention on July 18, 2026. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as a working-class Michigander and father running outside a career in politics.

background.text: In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as a working-class Michigander, a father and an ordinary citizen, and says he is not a career politician.
